title: Young life: Packing up my twenties flat-share experience
gist: Alice Garnett, a 26-year-old London writer, reflects on leaving a Canary Wharf flatshare for a Hackney Wick warehouse conversion with her boyfriend and a married couple. She describes flatsharing friendship as a uniquely valuable form of wellbeing amid a London life marked by redundancies and depressive episodes.

insights.claim: The author, 26, is moving from a Canary Wharf flatshare with her best friend to a Hackney Wick warehouse conversion shared with her boyfriend and a married couple.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Illustrates young Londoners sharing housing even into coupled and married life, consistent with high rental costs.

insights.claim: The author characterises Canary Wharf as dominated by suited finance workers and Hackney Wick by startup entrepreneurs by day and DJs by night.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Anecdotal picture of the demographic split between London's finance and creative-startup districts.
insights.quote: where suited finance bros will be supplanted by startup entrepreneurs (by day) and DJs (by night)

insights.claim: A married friend securing her first London rental and cohabiting with friends is framed as a step toward grownup life, showing shared living persisting past traditional milestones.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Shared living among couples signals affordability pressure in the London rental market.

insights.claim: The author argues that low-cost nights in with flatmates, such as popcorn, an £8 bottle of vinho verde and reality TV, are the best form of self-care.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Points to low-cost home entertainment as central to young adults' social lives.
insights.quote: there is nothing better for your wellbeing than microwaved popcorn, an £8 bottle of vinho verde and reality TV with your mates
insights.locator: But it’s not all funny anecdotes

insights.claim: The author's London years included two redundancies and half a dozen depressive episodes, reflecting job insecurity among young city workers.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Anecdotal evidence of employment precarity and mental-health strain among young Londoners.
insights.quote: my London years have involved some staggering lows, including two redundancies and half a dozen depressive episodes

insights.claim: The author's early-twenties London life centred on dating apps like Tinder, night buses and late-night fast food, which she expects to leave behind as she approaches 30.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Lifestyle transition at ~30 shifts consumer spending away from nightlife toward domestic life.
